title: UK equity financial statement API: annual and half-year figures for 1,000 London-listed companies
author: selfsideUK
selftext:
I run Selfside, a UK equity research site, and this is its data API. It serves income statements, balance sheets and cash flows for about 1,000 London-listed companies, annual and half-year.

A free account covers every company and includes 100 statement queries. Generate a key here: [https://selfside.co.uk/account/api](https://selfside.co.uk/account/api)

This is a V0 preview, with a stable release coming soon. The V1 release will have more data, like intra-year share counts, ownership data, derived metrics, and point-in-time queries to eliminate look-ahead bias during modelling.

To see a response before signing up, the token demo works for HSBC (HSBA), BAE Systems (BA) and Rolls-Royce (RR):

curl "[https://selfside.co.uk/api/v0/statements/HSBA:income\_statement:annual:2025-12-31?api\_token=demo](https://selfside.co.uk/api/v0/statements/HSBA:income_statement:annual:2025-12-31?api_token=demo)"

More product information and some benchmarks and examples be found at: [https://selfside.co.uk/data](https://selfside.co.uk/data)

If anyone is interested in UK equity market data and/or the stable release please reach out.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: I'd wait for point-in-time before modelling on this. restated figures look identical to the originals in a backtest, and that's where the leak comes from. will V1 keep the as-first-reported numbers next to the restated ones?

replies.author: selfsideUK
replies.body:
Yes this is not a stable release to be built on top of yet either, as well as not having all the functionality the V1 will have. Right now we're trying to gauge interest, as well as get feedback on existing response schema etc.

As filed and restated values will be kept, the current approach would be to use a date parameter in the query to return the latest value known as of that query date.

However, what would be more useful: a date query parameter that returns the statement as it stood on that day, or the first-reported and latest values together in one response? This is the sort of product guidance we're looking for ahead of V1.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the as-of date parameter, if I had to pick one. it's the question a backtest actually asks: what was known on this day. both values in one response is nice for auditing, but it leaves everyone to rebuild the as-of logic themselves and some will get it wrong. I'd also put the publication date on every value.

replies.author: selfsideUK
replies.body: Yeah this is the design so far. Everything will have an announcement date attached, but yes, the \`as\_of\` query is returning a single key by deduplicating with \`max(announced\_at)\` for a given key.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: one thing to test in that dedupe: filter to announced_at on or before as_of first, then take the max. if the max runs over all rows and the filter comes after, a later restatement makes the key vanish for every earlier date. will try it when V1 is out.

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body:
If the 1,000 companies are the ones listed today, a backtest on them has survivorship built in. UK names get delisted, taken over or moved to AIM all the time, and those are often the worst performers, so including dead and delisted companies matters as much as the point-in-time dates.

Another trap with annual plus half-year data: when people build trailing 12 month figures from H1 and FY reports, it's easy to mix a restated FY number with an original H1 number. Keeping both original and restated values, each with its own publication date, would make it much more useful for backtesting.

replies.author: selfsideUK
replies.body:
Yes, currently not survivorship-bias free. We do have delisted names in the backend currently, but historical coverage is not production ready and so is not served. It is something I feel confident we can provide good mitigations for. This project was originally started with backtesting as the goal so ensuring the dataset meets that bar for possible internal modelling is absolutely on the roadmap. 

The H2 derivation on restatements is something I was looking into recently and trying to resolve. The \`as\_of\` query parameter coming in V1 gives point-in-time access, so a backtest would see an H2 derived on a consistent basis.

Resolving the latest view of data, i.e., \`as\_of=now\` is slightly harder. H2 is re-derived whenever the full year or the first half is reprinted, such that H1 + H2 always sums to the latest FY. If only one of the two has been restated, that H2 mixes a restated figure with an originally reported one. However, these are additive operations, where a new H2 values is given the same \`announced\_at\` as the restated H1/FY so the vintage is fully preserved.

The impact was measured and is limited. Only H2 values are derived and so can be impacted. I tested freezing H2 at its first derivation instead, it improved some cases and worsened about as many, so the added complexity did not buy more correct data. It will remain a transparent limitation.   
  
See the comments in the other thread about serving restated and initially reported values with their announcement dates and whether you think the serving approach is the right direction.

replies.author: AoideusWasBanned
replies.body:
Freezing H2 and getting about as many cases worse as better makes sense, so keeping it as a documented limitation seems fair to me.

  
One cheap thing that would help backtests: a flag on each derived H2 saying whether its H1 and FY inputs come from the same vintage. Then people can drop or handle the mixed ones separately instead of finding them by hand.

  
On serving, original and restated side by side with their announcement dates is the right direction imo. Most fundamentals bugs I've seen in backtests come from using a number before it was actually published, so \`\_as\_of\` keyed on the announcement date rather than the period end covers most of it.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Point-in-time data is the part that matters most for anyone backtesting on fundamentals. If a statement is stamped with the date it was announced, you avoid the look-ahead bias where a model "knows" results before they were public. Half-year figures will help too, since a model that only sees annual results reacts slowly. I'd also check how restated numbers are handled, because a company can revise past figures and the old and new versions can give different backtest results.

replies.author: selfsideUK
replies.body:
Yeah this data will be point-in-time with "as of" queries, i.e., "give me these fundamentals know as of date X", as well as having the publication date attached to all values as part of the metadata. 

There's a lot of extra context about what this will look like (in the V1 stable release) in the other comment threads, please take a look!
